seo.title: TablePro for iPhone and iPad
seo.description: A free database client for iPhone and iPad. Connect to MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle and more over SSH or TLS, then browse, edit and query tables.

hero.title: TablePro for iPhone and iPad
hero.lead: Browse supported tables, run queries and edit rows on your phone or tablet.
hero.mac: Looking for the Mac app? <download>Download TablePro for Mac</download>.

databases.title: Databases
databases.lead: Create connections to these databases. All drivers are built in.
databases.syncedOnly: {engines} connections open when they come from your Mac, through iCloud Sync or a .tablepro file. You can’t create one in this app.
databases.others: Other connections synced from the Mac appear in your list but cannot open without a supported driver. See all <databases>supported databases</databases>.
databases.files: SQLite copies your chosen file into app storage; edits change that copy. You can also create a database. DuckDB opens a file in place or runs in memory.
databases.redis: Redis supports commands in the Query tab, not key browsing.
databases.sample: To look around first, open Chinook, the sample database that comes with the app.

browse.title: Browse and edit tables
paragraphs: Each connection has tabs for tables, queries, history and connection details.
Browse row cards, sort columns, search non-binary values and combine filters with AND or OR. Tap a foreign key to preview the referenced row. Structure lists columns, indexes and foreign keys.
Open a row to edit values or set NULL, then confirm the save. Insert and delete rows, or truncate and drop tables. Row edits and deletions require a primary key. Read-Only blocks changes.

query.title: Run queries
paragraphs: Write SQL with syntax highlighting, run or stop it, and share results as JSON, CSV or SQL INSERT statements. Use the clipboard or share sheet.
Results keep up to {results} rows; use LIMIT for large queries. History keeps the last {history} queries across connections on this device and does not sync.

Live Activities show elapsed time and rows received on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island. They also show SQL on the Lock Screen and expanded Island unless <ui>Settings > Live Activities > Hide Query</ui> is on.

security.title: Connect securely
paragraphs: SSH tunnels use a password or private key, with an optional passphrase. Import or paste the key. The app asks you to trust the server’s host key fingerprint on first connection.

TLS settings are per connection. MySQL, MariaDB, TiDB, OceanBase and PostgreSQL can verify certificates and hostnames and use client certificates. Redis supports certificate verification and client certificates. SQL Server’s Required mode encrypts without certificate verification. Certificates stay on this device.
Passwords and pasted keys stay in the Keychain. Synced SQL Server connections can use Microsoft Entra ID, not Windows authentication. Allow Local Network access to reach .local hosts.

safeMode.title: Safe Mode and app lock
paragraphs: Choose a level per connection: {levels}. Confirm Writes asks before writes; Read-Only blocks them. Unrecognized statements count as writes.
Set the level under Organization, and the default for new connections in Settings. Shortcuts follow the same level.
Enable Face ID or Touch ID in <ui>Settings > Security</ui>, with passcode fallback. The app locks on launch and after your chosen Auto-Lock interval.

ipad.title: On iPad
paragraphs: On iPad, use any orientation and multiple windows with Stage Manager or Split View. The tab bar can become a sidebar.
Keyboard shortcuts include ⌘1–⌘4 for tabs, ⌘F to search, ⌘↩ to run a query and ⌘N for a new connection. Mouse and trackpad work too.

mac.title: With your Mac
paragraphs: Enable iCloud Sync to share connections, groups and tags through your own iCloud account. Passwords need Sync Passwords enabled separately. Saved queries, SSH profiles and settings sync only between Macs.
Sync is free here; the Mac needs Starter or Team. See <pricing>pricing</pricing>.

Or transfer a .tablepro file through AirDrop or Files. Exports exclude passwords unless you include them and encrypt with a passphrase. Both options are free here; encrypted export needs a paid license on the Mac.
With sync enabled, Handoff continues an open connection or table on another device. See <sync>Sync and teams</sync>.

automation.title: Shortcuts, widgets and Spotlight
paragraphs: Use Siri or Shortcuts to open connections. Add Row to Table and Add Rows to Table insert JSON or CSV without opening the app. These actions do not run while the device is locked, follow Safe Mode and do not support Redis.
Quick Connect widgets open your first connections from the Home Screen. Connections also appear in Spotlight.

limits.title: Not on iPhone and iPad
limits.lead: These are in TablePro for Mac only:
items: The AI assistant and the MCP server
Saved queries, autocomplete, query formatting and EXPLAIN
Schema changes beyond truncating or dropping a table, and ER diagrams
Compare & Sync, Query Insights, Result Charts and Data Rewind
Exporting files in formats such as XLSX, and importing files into a table (Shortcuts can add rows)
The server dashboard, users and roles, and backups
SSH jump hosts, SSH agents and Windows authentication for SQL Server

knownIssues.title: Known issues in version {version}
items: In the row editor, don’t save a row while a long text or binary value shows shortened: the editor can write the shortened text over the full value. Change those rows on the Mac.
Saving a synced connection on iPhone or iPad can drop settings only the Mac uses, such as SSH jump hosts, and can lower its Safe Mode level. Edit those connections on the Mac.
When Redis connections verify the server’s certificate, they check the certificate and not the host name.
In the Shortcuts actions that add rows, CSV must be UTF-8 text with LF line endings.

privacy.title: Privacy
paragraphs: Usage reporting is off by default. Enable Share Usage Data in <ui>Settings > Privacy</ui> to send a daily report: hashed device ID, app and iOS versions, architecture, language, database types, connection count and first-use dates. No hostnames, usernames, passwords, queries or rows.
No license, update or plugin checks go to TablePro. Queries go to your databases, iCloud Sync to your iCloud account and Entra sign-in to Microsoft. Read the <privacyIos>privacy policy</privacyIos>.

get.title: Get TablePro for iPhone and iPad
get.source: The app is open source under the AGPLv3, in the <source>same repository</source> as the Mac app.

faq.question: Do I need the Mac app?
faq.answer: No. The iPhone and iPad app works on its own. If you also use a Mac, iCloud Sync and Handoff connect the two.

faq.question: Does it need a license?
faq.answer: No. The app has no paid features, no in-app purchases and no license. iCloud Sync is free here; only the Mac needs a Starter or Team license to sync.

faq.question: Is it the same as the Mac app?
faq.answer: No. It has a smaller feature set. See <iosLimits>features not available here</iosLimits>.
